overall.one_line_summary: The frozen A2 preparation package is internally guarded, but it is not ready for LO because the operational executor is absent and measured A2 remains locked.
strengths: Immutable 52-candidate bindings and arm roles replay under focused validation.
Fresh provider, budget, TTL, isolated-root, protected-boundary, and safe-return requirements are explicit and fail closed.
The package preserves zero measured A2, REP-DEV, Selection, and Final exposure.
weaknesses: The current runner is an in-memory readiness state machine and has no production process/provider executor.
Production train evaluation and result receipts are not implemented; current helpers accept synthetic fixtures only.
The active measured authorization remains false and the standing D1 record has historical SCOPE/P1/P2 scope.

strengths: The package binds the A1 measured source, A2 candidate freeze, budget model, and lifecycle evidence needed for readiness.
weaknesses: No production measured-result path exists to substantiate future A2 journal claims.
suggestions: Implement an aggregate-safe production evaluator and claim-evidence receipt chain before LO.

strengths: Hard stops cover stale or partial quote, hash drift, incomplete coverage, exact ties, protected output, and lifecycle failure.
weaknesses: Several hard stops are library contracts rather than exercised operational controls.
suggestions: Add end-to-end failure-injection tests around the real orchestrator.

strengths: The package consistently labels readiness as engineering evidence and keeps measured A2, A3, Selection, and Final closed.
weaknesses: PLAN and HANDOFF previously routed directly to LO despite the executor gap.
suggestions: Use the AP-to-IM routing recorded in docs/audit/A2_PER_ARM_AUTOINDEX_audit_001.md.

strengths: Freeze, admission, adoption, staging, and safe-return concepts form a clear intended lifecycle.
weaknesses: The lifecycle narrative reaches external execution, but the implementation explicitly starts no process and requires a missing injected executor.
suggestions: Implement one CLI/orchestrator whose state transitions and receipts match the runbook end to end.

strengths: The failed provider admission is preserved in the append-only ledger and is not reinterpreted as PASS.
weaknesses: Operational failed paths and recovery have not yet been exercised for A2.
suggestions: Preserve failure-injection, resume, and remote-attempt evidence in append-only checkpoints.

strengths: Candidate coverage, deterministic tie rejection, diagnostic-arm non-advancement, budget, and evidence schemas are predeclared.
weaknesses: There is no production measured evaluator, exact-coverage runner, operational watchdog, or safe-return closeout path.
suggestions: Complete and validate the production execution path before any measured authorization or journal claim.

findings.observation: The runner is an in-memory state machine, starts no process or provider call, and has no executor of its own.
findings.reasoning: LO cannot execute or recover A2 from the current package, so direct LO routing would spend provider time without an operational path.
findings.suggestion: Implement and failure-test a production CLI/orchestrator before LO.

findings.observation: Production callers are rejected and only explicitly marked synthetic fixtures can create readiness evaluation objects.
findings.reasoning: Synthetic evidence cannot become measured evidence or support journal claims.
findings.suggestion: Add a separate production adapter that validates complete frozen output and emits aggregate-safe canonical receipts.

findings.observation: Preparation, provider admission, adoption, and staging are authorized, but candidate evaluation and measured A2 are not.
findings.reasoning: IM may finish engineering and staging but cannot legally turn readiness into measured execution.
findings.suggestion: Return to AP after IM for an authority-consistent goal refresh; do not mutate Owner decisions or invent a micro-gate.
